title: PFL World Tournament: Brand Development
tagline: A brand world for the PFL's new World Tournament — built so every fight felt like it mattered.

body: The PFL was launching a new World Tournament format and needed fans to understand — and care about — what was at stake. The brief called for bold 3D visuals across the fight clock and key on-screen elements, a sense of the tournament's global reach, and above all a bracket that felt like a central character, carrying the story from fight to fight.

Midway through, the tournament's structure and narrative changed completely. The system we'd been building, while on-brand, was designed for a different product, so we had to pivot fast once the new format was locked.

As Creative Director, I led a one-month concept phase and a three-month execution, delivering 100+ custom assets across the broadcast, the brand campaign and promotional content — so fans met one consistent tournament brand whether they were watching a fight, scrolling social or catching a promo.

We created the line “ONE SHOT” to capture the tournament's win-or-go-home stakes. It became the campaign's organizing idea, woven through the marketing and built into every on-screen element, so the brand message and the viewing experience told the same story.

impact.note: The client was thrilled, and fans across social media praised the modern, sleek look — 100+ assets that gave the new format one recognizable identity across broadcast, campaign and promo.
